dialogue.spoken_text: Hi! Let's count Fibonacci numbers, and watch each new number take shape.
We start with zero and one. These are our two starting values.
To make the next number, add the previous two. Then use the newest pair, and do it again.
The small labels tell us each number's place. We start at F zero, so F two is the third entry.
The older value sits on the left. The newer value sits beside it. Their labels move with them.
Listen for plus and equals. The answer appears when we say its name, and becomes our newest value.
Number windows show values, not piles of things. A window marked one thousand stands for that value, not one thousand objects.
We'll keep adding until the sequence first passes one hundred million. The numbers grow, but the rule stays the same.
zero plus one equals
There are two ones in a row. One is a starting value; the next was made by adding zero and one.
They have the same value, but different places. Keep both entries, because each belongs to the sequence.
one plus one equals
one plus two equals
two plus three equals
three plus five equals
five plus eight equals
eight plus thirteen equals
Let's look inside that addition. In the ones column, eight plus three makes eleven: one stays here, and one ten moves left.
That carried ten joins the ten already there. The columns now show two tens and one one. Then the newest pair moves on.
thirteen plus twenty-one equals
twenty-one plus thirty-four equals
thirty-four plus fifty-five equals
fifty-five plus eighty-nine equals
eighty-nine plus one hundred forty-four equals
Here the ones make thirteen. Write three and carry one ten. The tens, including that carry, also make thirteen.
Write three tens, and carry one hundred. That hundred joins the hundred already there. Every column keeps its own place.
one hundred forty-four plus two hundred thirty-three equals
two hundred thirty-three plus three hundred seventy-seven equals
three hundred seventy-seven plus six hundred ten equals
six hundred ten plus nine hundred eighty-seven equals
nine hundred eighty-seven plus one thousand five hundred ninety-seven equals
Now the values reach into the thousands. Start at the ones and follow each carry to the next column, one place at a time.
Seven plus seven makes fourteen. Next come eighteen tens, then fifteen hundreds. Each carry moves one column left; it never skips a place.

two thousand five hundred eighty-four plus four thousand one hundred eighty-one equals
four thousand one hundred eighty-one plus six thousand seven hundred sixty-five equals
six thousand seven hundred sixty-five plus ten thousand nine hundred forty-six equals
ten thousand nine hundred forty-six plus seventeen thousand seven hundred eleven equals
seventeen thousand seven hundred eleven plus twenty-eight thousand six hundred fifty-seven equals
twenty-eight thousand six hundred fifty-seven plus forty-six thousand three hundred sixty-eight equals
forty-six thousand three hundred sixty-eight plus seventy-five thousand twenty-five equals
The commas help us read groups of three digits. They are separators, not extra digits, and they do not change the addition.
Keep the ones columns lined up on the right. Even with larger numbers, each column still adds the same kind of units.

We have reached the final pair for this journey. Both values are below one hundred million. Their sum will cross that mark.
Watch the labels as the two values enter the formula. It is the same addition we used at the start, with more place-value columns.
thirty-nine million eighty-eight thousand one hundred sixty-nine plus sixty-three million two hundred forty-five thousand nine hundred eighty-six equals
We've counted forty-one entries, from F zero through F forty. Two starting values, then thirty-nine additions brought us here.
The newest number is just past one hundred million. We stop here today, but the rule can keep making more numbers.
Remember the motion: take the previous two, add them, keep the newest pair, and repeat. Every new entry has a place in the chain.
Thanks for counting with me. See you next time!
